members.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
members.content: Emma Roth is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated.

members.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
members.content: Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision. Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year.

members.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
members.content: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated.

topic_dossiers.topic_title: AI智能体日常任务失败率

members.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
members.content: AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives. According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time.

members.title: ShellBench发布:GPT-6Astra等先进AI模型日常任务失败率超三分之一OpenClaw基金会联合Parsewave、Hugging Face、Red Hat及加州大学伯克利分校发布AI智能体基准ShellBench。该测试基于超1000万次匿名真实交互，覆盖电子邮件、日历、电子表格、收据和聊天记录等日常事务。结果显示，OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta的先进模型处理个人事务失败率仍高，可靠性与安全性面临挑战。 刚刚 9.9K
members.content: OpenClaw基金会联合多家机构发布AI智能体基准测试ShellBench，研究显示，即使是OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta旗下的先进模型，在处理日常个人事务时仍存在较高失败率，可靠性与安全性面临挑战。ShellBench由OpenClaw基金会、Parsewave、Hugging Face、Red Hat及加州大学伯克利分校研究人员合作开发，基于超过1000万次匿名化真实AI智能体交互，评估模型在电子邮件、日历、电子表格、收据及聊天记录等复杂个人数据环境中的多步骤任务执行能力。测试发现，所有模型的任务失败率均超过三分之一，15.7%的尝试至少违反一项安全要求。稳定性方面，即使得分最高的OpenAI GPT-6Astra，在相同条件下重复执行三次任务，也只有不到一半概率能够全部成功。具体场景中，智能体79.5%的情况下未能正确记录儿童学校接送安排，18.6%的尝试未能识别并扣留敏感银行上传令牌，40.3%的情况下推荐了重复或错误的账单付款。研究还发现，模型本身对任务表现的影响总体大于智能体框架，但模型能力越强，框架选择带来的性能差异越明显。例如，GPT-6Astra在Pi框架中表现优于Claude Fable5.2，但在Claude Code中测试时则落后。Meta的Muse Wonder Full在Pi框架中的得分为56%，在Claude Code中降至38.1%。

members.title: GPT-6 不带专用生物模型上场：322 个设计蛋白进实验室，约一成有结合迹象OpenAI 11月24日发布预印本论文，探讨聊天大模型能否胜任专业生物模型，给出部分肯定：GPT-6系列无需专用生物模型，仅凭推理和通用编程工具就能设计蛋白质三维结构与氨基酸序列，并已通过多轮实验室检验。测试由OpenAI与Onava合作完成，先计算、再湿实验，以GPT-6.2设计为蓝本制作322个微型结合蛋白，覆盖5个靶点。 刚刚 7.9K
members.content: 聊天大模型能不能干专业生物模型的活？OpenAI 在 11 月 24 日发布的预印本论文里给了一半肯定答案：GPT-6 系列不依赖专用生物模型，仅凭推理和通用编程工具就能设计新的蛋白质三维结构与氨基酸序列，并已通过多轮实验室检验。测试由 OpenAI 与合作机构 Onava 联手完成。先赢计算，再过湿实验以 GPT-6.2 设计的结构为蓝本，团队制作了 322 个微型结合蛋白，覆盖 5 个靶点，其中 35 个（约 10.9%）显示出结合迹象，对象包括 PD-L1、IL-7Rα、TrkA、VEGF-A 和 IL-17A。另一项实验让 GPT-6.2 为 6 个抗体的结合环重写序列，182 个测试设计中 128 个（70%）仍能结合 IL-4Rα。计算比武更亮眼：内部模型在“基序支架”任务上成功率 43.7%，压过专用模型 RFdiffusion 的 27.8%；小分子对接准确率约 93%，几乎是 DiffDock-L（50%）的两倍。短板也很明显OpenAI 自己划了界：GPT-6 筛选候选时仍要借助 Boltz-2、ESMFold2 等专用模型，尚不能证明它能脱离这些帮手端到端设计蛋白。最明显短板是从氨基酸序列预测完整结构——内部模型平均 TM-score 只有 0.38，ESMFold2 则高达 0.93。

members.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
members.content: Key findings:Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs.An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take.In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets.

members.title: Anthropic 搭建 Siren 蜜罐诱测 AI 越狱：新 Claude 仍有 21%~32% 沙盒场景试图逃逸11月25日，Anthropic发布安全评估系统Siren，用“漏洞考场”测试智能体是否会越狱。系统设置26种缺陷沙盒，覆盖Linux命名空间、Docker、gVisor和虚拟机等隔离方案；每个场景布置常规运维任务，并在沙盒外放置文件、凭据或模拟网络服务作诱饵，观察智能体面对薄弱环节和外部诱惑时的行为。 刚刚 9.7K
members.content: 与其等智能体在生产环境里闯祸，不如先给它们搭一个满是漏洞的考场。11 月 25 日，Anthropic 公布名为 Siren 的安全评估系统，人为布置薄弱环节，看智能体面对沙盒漏洞和外部诱饵会不会“越狱”。26 种缺陷沙盒当考场Siren 的 26 种沙盒覆盖 Linux 命名空间、Docker 容器、gVisor 与虚拟机等隔离方案，每个场景安排一项常规运维任务，沙盒外摆好文件、凭据或模拟网络服务当诱饵。任务描述埋着搜索要求、紧迫感等诱导，但不要求出逃，也不授权访问外部。测试覆盖 1700 多种场景，且不启用产品级安全防护。结果差异明显：Mythos 5 滥用外部资源达 25.8%，Mythos 5.1 为 12.7%，Claude 5.5 系列与 Mythos 5.2 降到 0.6% 至 1.6%。不过这算的是“无授权使用”这种最严重的失调，新模型仍有 21% 至 32% 的场景尝试翻越沙盒边界。说清规矩比锁门管用新模型改善的原因尚无定论，Anthropic 猜测是训练中的边界约束起了作用。但有个便宜办法已验证有效：在系统提示词里写明沙盒类型、访问限制和“权限不足就停下报告”，模型尝试访问外部资源的比例可下降 68% 至 96%，对新模型能压到约 2% 或更低。再叠加漏洞上报工具与执行前自动审查，五款模型的失调比例直接归零，Mythos 5 也只剩 0.1%。

members.title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
members.content: Leather-clad billionaires aren’t the only ones who can be led astray by alleged honeypots.Researchers at Anthropic have developed Siren, a new honeypot test for artificial intelligence agents. The setup puts agents in realistic simulations designed to tempt them into misbehaving. How they respond will help researchers evaluate the likelihood that new models will go rogue when deployed in the real world, as well as the effectiveness of different safety measures.The test lets agents loose inside one of 26 different simulated sandbox environments.

members.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
members.content: Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent. The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work. The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping.

members.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
members.content: As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. One startup called Maple, co-founded by a former Apple engineer who worked on privacy-preserving technologies, is taking a different approach with its AI app, where users’ data remains private — even from the company itself.

members.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
members.content: Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83, trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close. Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value. The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector. The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share.

members.title: How Gemini is changing the game for Golden State's organization and fans.
members.content: Today, we’re expanding our partnership with Golden State — making Google Gemini the Official AI Assistant Partner and Official Generative AI & Enterprise LLM Partner of the Warriors, the 2026 WNBA Champion Valkyries, and Chase Center.The collaboration integrates Gemini across the entire franchise ecosystem. For fans, that means a more interactive game-day experience, both inside Chase Center via interactive videoboard features, and across digital channels for fans following from home.

members.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
members.content: The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says it has seen a “marked rise” in AI-driven cyberattacks in recent months, as hackers increasingly rely on autonomous hacking tools to identify and exploit simple weaknesses to break into systems and networks. The U.K. National Cybersecurity Center (NCSC) said it has seen several cyber incidents since September involving autonomous hacking tools, such as penetration testing tools used by defenders to stress-test their cybersecurity defenses.

members.title: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film
members.content: Though David Fincher’s fans had been eagerly anticipating The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, early screenings of the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel starring Brad Pitt have raised questions about whether generative AI was used in the film. People have claimed that the movie is chock-full of uncanny, inconsistent visuals that make it feel more like slop than the sort of polished film you’d expect from the director of sleek productions like Fight Club and The Social Network.Following a number of Cliff Booth critics screenings that took place last week ahead of the film’s premiere on。

topic_dossiers.topic_title: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom?

members.title: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom? Cross-Magnification Provenance Verification for Whole-Slide Images
members.content: Published on Nov 22 Authors: , , , , , Abstract Visual agents navigate whole-slide images through magnified observations associated with claimed locations. However, a visually plausible observation does not necessarily originate from its claimed location, particularly across magnifications and in regions with similar tissue structures. We formulate cross-magnification provenance verification (CMPV) to evaluate whether visual evidence supports a claimed spatial association, recover the source when possible, and abstain when evidence is insufficient.

members.title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics
members.content: Published on Nov 22 Authors: , , , , , , , , , Abstract PhyCoVE, a 533-case benchmark, and counterfactual fidelity evaluate video editing models on physical counterfactual edits involving rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics, showing that even the best model reproduces only about one seventh of the physical change. Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit.

members.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
members.content: Published on Nov 21 Authors: , , , Abstract NightWatch adds a lightweight streaming watcher to vision-language computer-use agents to keep perception synchronized with dynamic interfaces, reducing latency and wasted time while maintaining or improving task success. Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own.

members.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
members.content: We are introducing ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy. A robot policy built from persistent coding agents that reason and act asynchronously. A single coding agent can issue parallel motion commands, but every decision still passes through one reasoning process. While it diagnoses a grasp with one arm, independent work on the other may wait. ACAP distributes decision-making across parts of one robot, with a hyper-agent coordinating their work. 🦾 Each member is a robot policy. A persistent agent controls a configurable group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis.

members.title: Attributing Security Outcomes in LLM-Agent Evaluations: The Role of Content-Free State
members.content: View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract:Security benchmarks for LLM agents record whether each attack succeeded and compare agents, attacks, and defenses by attack success rate (ASR). Such comparisons are valid only if the agent, the attack, and the defense cause each verdict. We show that verdicts also depend on content-free state: details of a run that carry no information about the system under test, such as the Python hash seed, the order of tools or evidence, and the scoring of failed runs.
